messages:
maria: Heads up — after last kernel+driver push in eu-west-1 we saw a clear uptick in Xid events, started ~1717642000, affecting ~5-7% of cards across 3 racks. A few hosts auto-drained. Low severity but causing capacity loss and retry storms.

jon: How many Xid types are we seeing? ECC too or just Xid spikes?

maria: Mostly Xid 79 and Xid 13. Some ECC counters ticked on two hosts. Example dmesg around crash: 
```
[ 6558.123456] NVRM: Xid (79): 9 0 0x00000000 0x00000000 0x00000000
[ 6558.123460] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 6558.124000] kernel: pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Corrected error received: id 00e7
```

kevin: PCIe AER corrected errors alongside Xid. Grafana shows link retrain spikes starting at the kernel rollout window. Link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abc (log)

infra-oncall-bot: Hosts auto-drained: host-eu-west-234, host-eu-west-237, host-eu-west-241. Drain reason: gpu-health xiddetected.

dave: Capacity hit estimated ~5% for eu-west. Short-term we should steer batch workloads to us-west to keep latency-critical infra unaffected. That will raise cross-region egress cost ~+8% for next 24h.

sre-lead: Proposed mitigation plan: pause rollout, run rollback on a small canary subset (10% of eu-west GPUs), enable deeper burn-in + nvml logging on drained hosts, and collect PCIe/AER counters. If rollback reduces Xid rate we proceed incremental.

jon: Agreed. Can we query telemetry quickly? Use this PromQL to show Xid rate per AZ: 
```promql
sum(rate(gpu_xid_errors_total[5m])) by (az)
```
This already shows eu-west-1a >> eu-west-1b.

maria: I'm creating a rollback PR and scheduling a rollback canary 23:00 UTC. Will also flip on verbose NVML logging on the canary hosts.

maria: Quick triage notes I pushed to the ticket: correlation with kernel 6.1.12-rt and driver 535.86, increased pcie retrain and corrected AER. No obvious temperature/thermal trends on fail hosts.

kevin: Question: try kernel param `pci=nomsi` or `pcie_aspm=off` in canary? Might reduce retrain noise. But let's rollback first to be conservative.

jon: Also worth checking BIOS PCIe link training firmware versions on the affected hosts — some vendors shipped a microcode that regresses under new kernels.

infra-oncall-bot: Canary rollback plan created: rollback-group-eu-west-10pct, start 1717650000, rollback window 30m.

deploy-bot: PR #3421 created by maria to revert kernel package on canary hosts. Link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/3421

dave: If rollback doesn't help, plan B = pin to older driver + kernel, increase burnin to 6h for suspect cards, escalate to vendor RMA for persistent ECC. Need cost approval for temporary extra reserved capacity if we lose >10%.

maria: I'll run these local commands on affected hosts and attach output to the ticket (nvml/nvmlp logs): 
```
sudo dmesg | grep -i -E "NVRM|Xid|PCIe|AER" --color=never | tail -n 100
sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -o cat --since "2 hours ago"
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=err_state,temperature.gpu,memory.total --format=csv -q
```

jon: Also collect `lspci -vvv` and `ethtool -i` for the root complex.

kevin: I'll throttle non-essential background batch jobs in eu-west during the rollback window to reduce noise.

maria: Canary scheduled. Will post results in this thread. :thumbsup:

sre-lead: If canary shows >50% reduction in Xid per-host, resume controlled rollout with 5% increments and 1h observation windows. Otherwise hold and prepare rollback of full rollout.

maria: Initial canary done — early signal: Xid event rate on canary group dropped ~70% in the first 45m. Still collecting full 2h burnin. Will post logs and final verdict by 1717647134.

kevin: Nice. If burnin stays green, we'll stage a staggered rollback across remaining racks with 2h observation windows.

maria: Final: 2h burnin completed, telemetry shows sustained drop. Rolling back remaining eu-west hosts in waves; opening follow-up ticket for vendor BIOS checks on hosts that had persistent AER. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
